paragraphs: Friend, here's the biggest thing in this passage, and I want you to hear it LOUD: you are a child of God. The writer says, "Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are!" (1 John 3:1). That's not a nickname, and it's not a title on a sticker. It's who you ARE, and the world not recognizing you doesn't change it, because it did not know Him either.

And here's the part that keeps us standing tall. We're children of God right now, and "what we will be has not yet been revealed," but "when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is" (1 John 3:2). So the writer says to remain in Christ, so we can be confident and unashamed at His coming (1 John 2:28). Everyone who has this hope "purifies himself, just as Christ is pure" (1 John 3:3). That's a hope that gets you up and moving, friend, not one that lets you sit on the couch.

Now, the writer does not tiptoe about sin. He says Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin (1 John 3:5), and he says to let no one deceive you about who is righteous (1 John 3:7). He says the Son of God was revealed "to destroy the works of the devil" (1 John 3:8). A child of God refuses to practice sin, and that child loves his brother (1 John 3:9-10). So here's your takeaway, baker: lean on the Father's love, hold that hope, and let your life show whose child you are.
